project._uiFrameworkNote: React 18/19 + Tailwind v4. globals.css is a shadcn-shaped token export, so component variant vocabulary follows shadcn naming.

Input._note: Code implemented, CI-bound, and now RENDERED and visually verified in Storybook across all five states in both modes. Still draft: promotion to stable is storybook-chromatic-builder's call and there is no Chromatic baseline. Rendering caught a real bug (see the cn/tailwind-merge fix) and disproved part of the focus-ring rationale.

Accordion._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Figma models a SINGLE item; an Accordion is a group, so code takes items[] and openIds[] (an array, because several sections may be open at once, which the Figma State enum cannot express). The map types State as closed|open and Disabled as false|true string unions; both emitted as real booleans since a stringly-typed boolean is a Figma artefact not an API. Triggers are wrapped in headings for heading navigation - the difference from Collapsible. No focus token is recorded on this set; the shared ring treatment is asserted.

Alert Dialog._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Two deliberate differences from Dialog, both accessibility decisions: the backdrop does NOT dismiss (a decision dismissed by misclick is how people lose data; Escape still cancels), and description is REQUIRED by the type. Initial focus goes to Cancel so a reflexive Enter takes the safe path. No slots on purpose - a slot would let a caller turn it back into a Dialog. This component binds card-foreground, which is the CORRECT pairing for a card fill; Dialog/Drawer/Sheet bind plain foreground on the same fill.

Breadcrumb._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Figma models a FIXED three-level trail (Home/Parent/Current labels) because a design file cannot express a variable-length list; those three properties are one EXAMPLE of the array, not the API. Code takes items[]. GAPS: no token for the current page (everything binds muted-foreground, which would make the current page indistinguishable from its ancestors, so foreground is asserted), no separator token, no link/hover treatment. The collapse affordance is a real button with an accessible name, never an inert ellipsis - collapsing must not hide levels from assistive technology that a sighted user can reach.

Card._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE ONLY COMPONENT WHOSE CODE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MATCH ITS RECORD. Card.doc.json binds text to info-foreground, which is INVERTED relative to card-foreground (info-foreground is Light neutral/50 + Dark neutral/950; card-foreground is Light neutral/950 + Dark neutral/50). On a card fill that is near-white text on a white card in Light and near-black on near-black in Dark - contrast roughly 1:1, text invisible in BOTH modes. info-foreground is the light-on-dark pairing, correct for text on the SOLID info fill, which is how Badge uses it legitimately. Code binds card-foreground. Transcribing faithfully would ship a visible bug rather than a documentation inaccuracy. FIGMA OWES A REBIND; until then docs:adopt keeps re-importing the wrong token. Also transcribed-but-flagged: size/11 (smallest in the scale) for card text, and State=Interactive binding 2px primary, the same treatment Input uses for FOCUS, so an interactive card looks focused at rest.

Collapsible._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Token-identical to Accordion, and unlike the Drawer/Sheet pair this is DEFENSIBLE: the Figma master draws one disclosure item, which is exactly what a Collapsible is, while an Accordion is a group of the same item. The records match because the design file draws one thing. Difference is real in code - one boolean vs items[]/openIds[]. Trigger deliberately NOT wrapped in a heading: a lone Collapsible usually sits inside content that already has one.

Dialog._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 on the native <dialog> element via the shared internal components/modal-surface.tsx. showModal() supplies the focus trap, Escape, top layer and ::backdrop from the platform, following the NativeSelect precedent. children/footer are SLOTS not typed props, per the record's instruction that embedded copy must not be generated as a public code prop until engineering API review. GAPS: Size has no token backing (there are NO width or container tokens anywhere in the file - every size/* variable is a type size), and the backdrop has no token.

Drawer._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. See the Sheet note - the two are indistinguishable in the design file.

Field._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Owns the accessibility wiring (generates id, binds label-for/aria-describedby/aria-invalid) via a render prop rather than cloneElement, so injected props are type-checked at the call site. The Figma Value property has NO code equivalent — the control is a child, so Field owning a value would be a competing source of truth. KNOWN CONFLICT: Input/Textarea/NativeSelect each render their own errorMessage, so inside a Field the error must be passed to Field, not the control, or you get two messages and two live regions. KNOWN INCONSISTENCY, recorded not resolved: Field uses aria-live=polite per its record; Input uses role=alert. Both cannot be right; moving the three shipped controls needs its own review.

Hover Card._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Opens on focus as well as hover: the record is explicit that it must be reachable on keyboard focus or its content must exist elsewhere, since hover alone excludes keyboard and touch users. closeDelay lets the pointer travel from trigger into the card without it vanishing. Density is not just spacing - the record ties detailed density to supporting metadata, so density sets spacing and meta is the content it makes room for; meta without detailed renders nothing.

Label._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Two deliberate divergences from figma.map.json, both in Table 2: State is a boolean not a two-value enum (the record's own governance rule keeps visual State axes as story states, and every other control here uses disabled: boolean); and Type has THREE code states because most labels carry no marker at all and Figma has no variant for that, which the record's own dont requires. The marker is aria-hidden and deliberately not tinted destructive — tokensUsed records no marker colour.

Native Select._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from docs/components/native-select.md. The map lists controlled: ["open"] but Open was deliberately NOT emitted as a prop: a native select menu is platform-owned, cannot be opened programmatically, and Open binds tokens identical to Focus because the control is always focused while its menu is up. appearance-none is deliberately NOT set, so the platform draws its own indicator — tokensUsed carries no chevron colour and suppressing it would mean inventing a token that does not exist. Rendered and built in Storybook; not yet visually reviewed.

Popover._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Uses the CORRECT surface pairing (popover fill + popover-foreground text) - worth noting against Dialog which binds plain foreground on a card fill, and Card whose text token is outright wrong. Size has no width token (same gap as Dialog). PLACEMENT IS NOT COLLISION-AWARE: places on the requested side and stays there; flipping needs a positioning library, out of scope for a token-level component and recorded rather than half-built. The modal prop implements the record line exactly: a popover holding a form should trap focus, a non-modal one should not.

Popover / Backdrop._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE ONLY SCRIM TOKEN IN THE SYSTEM AND IT IS THE WRONG KIND. Binds fill foreground, which is neutral/950 Light and neutral/50 Dark - it INVERTS, giving a near-black scrim in Light (right) and a near-WHITE scrim in Dark (wrong). Dialog/Drawer/Sheet/AlertDialog record no backdrop token at all, which is why modal-surface.tsx falls back to raw black/50. So there is no correct scrim token anywhere. Applied as recorded because unlike Card it produces a visible functioning backdrop and deviating would mean inventing; FIGMA OWES an overlay/scrim token, which would close five gaps at once.

Popover / Close._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Defaults label to Close rather than requiring it, unlike TableActionTrigger where the name must identify a row - here Close genuinely is right almost every time and a required prop everyone fills identically is friction not safety. Binds radius/7, a half-step ramp member and the only component that uses it; written as an explicit calc so it can never degrade to a raw pixel value. No disabled tokens and no icon colour recorded.

Popover / Root Composition._note: DELIBERATELY NOT BOUND TO CODE, same treatment as Table / Root Composition: its Pattern axis is kind: story-only (Storybook story, never a prop). Its four patterns - Basic, Align, Form, RTL - ship as stories in components/popover.stories.tsx.

Popover / Viewport._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THIS WAS THE LAST UNRESOLVED DOC BLOCK IN THE SYSTEM - six variant meanings left deliberately owed because the side axis already holds top/right/bottom/left for placement and guessing would have put a wrong meaning in six blocks. Its own description settled it without a Figma query: direction is an ACTIVATION direction (data-activation-direction), not placement, and current/previous are the incoming and outgoing halves of a transition. Vocabulary added on that evidence; the system now has ZERO owed doc blocks. State deliberately did NOT become an enum: both halves render at once during a transition and an enum could only show one.

Segmented Tab._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. The item half of Tabs. Note the inversion: the SELECTED tab takes the lighter card fill and lifts out of the muted track rather than being highlighted, which only reads correctly inside the container. The map types Selected as a false|true string union; emitted as a real boolean. Focus ring is asserted from the record’s own prose ("focus remains visually distinguishable using the shared ring treatment") rather than transcribed from a binding. No disabled variant exists.

Separator._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. decorative has no Figma property and must exist: the record splits the component semantically with no visual difference, so Figma cannot express it. Defaults to decorative. A semantic vertical separator also sets aria-orientation, because role=separator implies horizontal.

Sheet._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. DRAWER AND SHEET ARE IDENTICAL IN EVERY RECORDED RESPECT: same tokensUsed, same state rows, same variant count, same props, same accessibility. The ONLY difference is the placement axis name (Drawer=Placement, Sheet=Side) with the same two values. The distinction exists only as prose. Both built as specified rather than merged because collapsing them is a design decision; they share modal-surface.tsx so they cannot drift further. UNRESOLVED - worth deciding: give them a real visual difference, or collapse them.

Table._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Figma's Selection axis is NOT a prop: selection belongs to a ROW (Table / Row carries State=Selected with a real accent fill), so a table-level selection prop would be a second source of truth. First/Second row label are example content, not API - same pattern as Breadcrumb's three fixed labels. DENSITY CARRIES NO TOKEN DELTA anywhere in this family, verified not assumed: Table / Row shows three Compact/Comfortable pairs and all three bind identical tokens, so row height is raw padding.

Table / Action Trigger._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. `label` is REQUIRED in the type on purpose: the record's accessibility contract demands 'a programmatic accessible name that identifies the action context (for example, Open row actions)', and making it optional would make it forgettable. GAPS: no disabled tokens and no icon colour are recorded; shared conventions asserted.

Table / Caption._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. The record: 'Position is visual; code should preserve caption semantics and reading order.' A <caption> must be the FIRST CHILD of <table> wherever it appears, so bottom placement uses caption-side and never DOM reordering - moving it would break the naming relationship.

Table / Cell._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. EMPHASIS CHANGES COLOUR, NOT WEIGHT, despite its name and despite the shared vocabulary calling it 'heavier weight'. The record binds foreground vs muted-foreground and no weight token; transcribed as bound, not as named. CONSEQUENCE WORTH REVIEWING: a DEFAULT cell is muted-foreground, so ordinary table data renders muted and only 'strong' cells get full contrast - backwards from the usual convention, and it affects every cell in every table.

Table / Container._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. Figma's Viewport axis is kind: responsive-fixture - the map itself says 'Not a prop unless code deliberately exposes one' - so overflow is plain CSS and takes no input. The scroll region is focusable AND named, because a region that scrolls but cannot be focused is unreachable by keyboard. GAP: the record binds size/10 (smallest in the file) on a wrapper that renders no text of its own, almost certainly inherited from a nested example; deliberately not applied.

Table / Head._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. `scope` has no Figma property but is required by the record's own prose ('use scope/row-header semantics in code where applicable'); a th without scope is ambiguous in any table with both row and column headers. GAP: no fill is recorded on the head cell - the header band's muted fill lives on Table / Row (Type=Header) - so TableHead used outside a header row would be transparent.

Table / Root Composition._note: DELIBERATELY NOT BOUND TO CODE. Its map entry has no real properties - Pattern is kind: story-only ("Storybook story, never a prop") and Viewport is kind: responsive-fixture. It is a set of composition examples, so it ships as the four stories in components/table.stories.tsx (Basic, Footer, Actions, RTL). Binding it would claim it is a component.

Table / Row._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. RECOVERED FROM THE 8-ROW CAP BY INFERENCE, not guesswork. 10 variants, 8 rows shown; the two missing are Header/Comfortable and Footer/Comfortable. Every Compact/Comfortable pair that IS present binds identical tokens (three pairs, three matches), so Density is proven inert in this record and the absent rows carry their Compact twins tokens. This does NOT generalise - it works because the missing rows sit on an axis proven inert by the rows that survived; Popover / Content shows 1 of 48 and stays blocked. ASSERTED: recorded hover binds only text, identical to resting, so a muted tint is added rather than transcribed. No focus token for a selectable row either.

Tabs._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. TABS AND SEGMENTED TAB ARE TWO HALVES OF ONE CONTROL. Tabs binds only a container fill (muted) and has NO selected-state treatment at all; Segmented Tab binds exactly that treatment and no container. Segmented Tab’s own description confirms it: "Place instances inside a secondary-colored segmented-control container." Neither is complete alone, so Tabs renders SegmentedTab items. Neither Orientation nor Density carries a token delta, so both are layout-only and Density uses raw padding (no spacing token is recorded). No focus token either; the shared ring is asserted.

Textarea._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026 from docs/components/textarea.md, which was transcribed rather than authored. Shares Input's visual contract token-for-token, so Input's three resolved build blockers were inherited, not re-decided. Focus is keyed on focus-visible: directly rather than has-[:focus-visible] because there is no wrapper — no slots means the focusable and bordered element are the same node. resize-none enforces the record's fixed-viewport sizing policy. The character counter is deliberately NOT a live region: polite announcement per keystroke is noise, so it is linked via aria-describedby and read on focus. Rendered and built in Storybook; not yet visually reviewed.

Toggle._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE RECORD’S ACCESSIBILITY CONTRACT WAS WRONG and was fixed: Toggle was mapped to the `choice` archetype, which told it to expose state via aria-checked and referenced radio-group arrow keys. A toggle button is the W3C APG Toggle Button pattern - aria-pressed, and both Space and Enter activate. Added a `togglebutton` archetype and remapped Toggle + Toggle Group, then re-enriched. THREE RECORDED ODDITIES, transcribed rather than corrected: (1) Pressed+hover binds the SAME tokens as pressed at rest, so a pressed toggle gives no hover feedback; (2) it binds radius/md where every other control in the system binds radius/lg; (3) Pressed+disabled loses the pressed state entirely and renders identically to unpressed+disabled - aria-pressed still reports it so assistive tech is correct, but a sighted user cannot tell. 8 variants is exactly at the 8-row cap, so nothing is truncated.

Toggle Group._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. THE RECORD IS ALMOST EMPTY - one state row and two tokens (accent-foreground, size/14) for four variants, the thinnest of any component built so far. And accent-foreground looks like a stray binding: it is the foreground for the accent fill, but the group binds no fill of its own, so it is a foreground token with nothing to sit on. The items (Toggle) already carry accent/accent-foreground for their pressed state. Implemented as a LAYOUT-ONLY container with each Toggle owning its appearance, which is what the tokens actually support. Figma owes either a real container treatment or the removal of that binding. role=group NOT radiogroup even in single mode, since members are toggle buttons; single mode has no must-have-one guard because all members may legitimately be off when they are actions.

Tooltip._note: Implemented 9 Aug 2026. label is deliberately a STRING not a ReactNode - everywhere else a content property was widened to a node, but the record calls this brief non-interactive and a node slot invites buttons and links into a surface unreachable by keyboard and invisible on touch. The narrow type is the guardrail. The fill/text inversion (foreground fill + card text) is CORRECT and deliberate; note it is the same foreground token that is wrong as a backdrop - as a fill behind short text it inverts correctly, as a full-screen scrim it inverts backwards.

repo._note: Single-package repo, not a monorepo. Docs were moved out of the bkit-style docs/02-design/ path to a flat docs/ on 9 Aug 2026 and narrowed to build-relevant content only; historical material (CRRT benchmark, the 8 Aug audit snapshot, the Figma cleanup backlog) moved to notes/. storybook._note: Storybook 9 + Vite + Tailwind v4 at the repo root, not in a monorepo. storybook-chromatic-builder expects a pnpm/Turborepo workspace with packages/tokens and packages/ui; this is the single-package equivalent. Chromatic deliberately deferred: it is a paid SaaS needing CI, and a baseline of one component carries little signal. Revisit once several components exist.

audit._percentSemanticNote: REPLACED the single unqualified `percentSemantic: 100` on 9 Aug 2026. These are THREE DENOMINATORS, not three estimates of one quantity, and all three are arithmetically correct: (a) 100 = color bindings in product surfaces reaching a role-named token, 11015/11015; (b) 99.7 = the same including the 30 documentation swatch frames on the '↳ Color' page, 11015/11045 — the old note truncated this to '99'; (c) 19 = share of ALL bindings sitting in the semantic 'Jake UI' collection, 12379/65045. (c) is NOT a quality measure: dimension and type bind straight to scale primitives by shadcn/Tailwind convention, so reading it as '81% unsemantic' is a category error. Note also that the right-sizing conclusion (rename-in-place + cleanup, not a rewrite) rests on bindingsUnresolved: 0, not on any of these three. Reasoning: docs/design-system/decisions/2026-08-09-percent-semantic-denominators.md

audit._tokenGapsFound: Found 9 Aug 2026 while building the overlay family. (1) NO width or container tokens exist in the file - every size/* variable is a type size (10-22) - so Dialog Size and Drawer/Sheet Width are raw values in code. (2) No backdrop/scrim token on any of the four overlay records. (3) SEMANTIC MISMATCH: Alert Dialog binds card-foreground while Dialog, Drawer and Sheet bind plain foreground, all on a card fill. Verified in .figma-tokens-dump.json that foreground and card-foreground currently resolve to the SAME primitives (neutral/950 Light, neutral/50 Dark), so this is invisible today - but it is the same latent failure mode already recorded for warning-muted-foreground, where identical-resolving tokens made a planned fix a no-op. card-foreground is the correct pairing for a card fill.
audit._tokenDefectsFound: CARD TEXT IS BOUND TO THE WRONG TOKEN - found 9 Aug 2026 while building batch 3. Card.doc.json binds text to info-foreground on a card fill. Verified in .figma-tokens-dump.json that info-foreground (Light neutral/50, Dark neutral/950) is INVERTED relative to card-foreground (Light neutral/950, Dark neutral/50). Result is roughly 1:1 contrast and invisible text in both modes. This is a live defect, not a latent one like the Dialog/AlertDialog foreground mismatch. Badge also binds info-foreground but legitimately, because Badge has a solid info fill and that is what the token is for. FIX: rebind Card text to card-foreground in Figma, then re-run docs:adopt. Until then the code deliberately diverges and docs/components/card.md is the only thing preventing someone re-transcribing the wrong value.
